intervals.label: SNOLAB: construction (DOE-approved)
intervals.note: Start: Symmetry Magazine article dated 2018-05-07 announcing DOE construction approval. End moved from 2026-03 to 2026-01 (base temperature reached in Jan 2026 per the July 2026 collaboration talk; SLAC announced it on 2026-03-17). Earlier basis: set where the collaboration's own materials describe installation as complete and cooldown/commissioning beginning (Fermilab CPC page: 'Installation was completed late last year'; SLAC news 2026-03-17: base temperature reached, moving into detector commissioning).
intervals.quote: The US Department of Energy has approved funding and start of construction for the SuperCDMS SNOLAB experiment, which will begin operations in the early 2020s.

intervals.label: SNOLAB: commissioning
intervals.locator: Light Dark World 2026 talk (29 July 2026), slide "SuperCDMS SNOLAB Cooldown"; corroborated by SLAC news, 2026-03-17
intervals.note: Start moved from 2026-03 to 2026-01: the collaboration's own July 2026 talk gives "Reached base temperature in Jan 2026" followed by "Detector characterization began", and SLAC (17 March 2026) says reaching base temperature marks the transition to commissioning ("With base temperature achieved, the collaboration has now moved into detector commissioning, a months-long process of turning on, calibrating and optimizing each detector channel."). 2026-03 was the date of the announcement. End set where the 2026-08-26 SLAC article reports the start of the early-science data-collection phase.

intervals.label: SNOLAB: early-science operations
intervals.note: Open interval. The same source states the early-science phase continues through fall 2026, followed by a warm-up/optimization period, then a full-sensitivity science run planned to start in 2027; those future phases are not separately recorded as they had not begun as of verified_at. Checked 2026-10-25: no source newer than the 2026-08-26 SLAC article was found. The July 2026 talk anticipated SR1a "to continue until Sept 2026", then a full warm-up with maintenance and repairs before SR1b in early 2027; SLAC says early science "will continue through fall 2026". The experiment may therefore already be warming up, which no fetched source reports, so it is not recorded as an event.
intervals.quote: has begun collecting its very first scientific data

intervals.label: SR1b: full-sensitivity science run (planned)
intervals.locator: Light Dark World 2026 talk, slide "SuperCDMS SNOLAB Science Run 1a/b"
intervals.note: A schedule, not a reported event. SLAC, 26 August 2026: the early-science phase is followed by a warm-up to optimize the cryogenic system and noise environment and "a year of data collection with the detectors running at optimized, full sensitivity"; the full-scale search is "set to begin in 2027". After SR1b: installation of water tanks and Science Run 2.

name: SuperCDMS
notes: This record covers only the SNOLAB programme (INSPIRE recid 1357671). The earlier Soudan-era programme (INSPIRE recid 1298909, FNAL-E-0891), which has its own completion date (2015-01-01) confirmed by Symmetry Magazine, is recorded as experiment:supercdms-soudan and linked here as the predecessor.
DOE Critical Decision milestones between the 2014 INSPIRE approval and the 2018 construction start (if any) are not recorded: no source consulted gives them.

physics_goals.quote: The collaboration is searching for dark matter particles with masses smaller than ten times the mass of the proton.
value: Detect dark matter particles with masses smaller than about ten times the mass of the proton via nuclear recoils in cryogenic silicon and germanium crystals

summary.plain: SuperCDMS SNOLAB looks for dark matter using silicon and germanium crystals cooled almost to absolute zero. It is the successor to an earlier version of the experiment that ran at the Soudan mine in Minnesota until 2015, and is now starting up nearly a mile underground at SNOLAB in Canada, aiming at very light dark matter particles.
summary.technical: Cryogenic Ge/Si ionization-and-phonon dark matter search at SNOLAB, succeeding the earlier SuperCDMS Soudan programme (experiment:supercdms-soudan, 2009-2015). Now under commissioning/early science with 24 detector crystals cooled to 15-30 mK, targeting sub-10-proton-mass WIMPs; full-sensitivity science operations are planned for 2027.

unique_capabilities.quote: For SuperCDMS, that temperature is just tens of millikelvins, or thousandths of a degree above absolute zero.
value: Phonon- and ionization-sensing cryogenic crystal detectors optimized for very low-mass WIMP nuclear recoils, operated near 15-30 mK
